newsitem.title: CANADA: Potash falls after takeover announcement.
newsitem.headline: Potash falls after takeover announcement.

text.p: Shares of Canadian fertilizer giant Potash Corp of Saskatchewan fell on Tuesday on the first day of trading after the company said it was buying U.S. nitrogen concern Arcadian Corp in a cash and stock deal.

The US$1.18 billion Potash bid, which eclipsed a proposed merger between Arcadian and Freeport-McMoRan Inc, was aimed at adding nitrogen to Potash's product slate, a move that would see it producing all three nutrients.
The definitive agreement was announced on the Monday Labor Day holiday. Potash fell 2.50 to 101 in Toronto and by 2-1/2 to 73-1/2 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Potash Corp, already a world powerhouse in potash and phosphate production, had long been speculated as a suitor for various nitrogen-based fertilizer producers.
Analysts on Tuesday said a US$25-million breakup fee that would be paid to Potash if the takeover failed to go ahead made the chances of another competing offer slim.
With Arcadian shares in New York trading at 24-3/8 on Tuesday, below the Potash offer of US$25 to US$27 per share, investors also appeared to be expecting no sweetened bid.
Vahid Fathi, analyst with Everen Securities in Chicago, said he downgraded Potash Corp on Tuesday to short-term market underperformer from short-term market performer following the acquisition news.
Fathi said that the addition of nitrogen, which is much more volatile in pricing than phosphate and potash, was likely to result in a price-earnings ratio for the company.
"This combination, I think, is going to exert downward pressure on the combination multiple that is eventually going to be assigned to Potash Corp following the inclusion of Arcadian," he said.

Where potash and phosphate producers tend to enjoy a more managed and stable market for their mined products, fortunes of nitrogen companies tend to rise and fall with the prices of their feedstock, natural gas and ammonia, he said.
"It has very volatile price behavior, historically at least, and frankly, I don't see any reason going forward for any changes in the volatility we see," Fathi said.
Arcadian, whose geographic strength is in the southeastern United States, is the western hemisphere's largest nitrogen fertilizer producer.
The move for Potash Corp follows a string of recent and planned acquisitions.
The company made two large phosphate purchases in the U.S. for a total of US$1.1 billion.
Potash also said last month it was in talks to buy BASF AG's 51-percent stake in German potash company Kali und Salz AG for about C$500 million. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
